chunks: And from him, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the greeting (salutation) in the two rak'ahs of Witr, so he said: 'You wake the sleeper and speak with the need (of the prayer).'

key_terms.التَّسْلِيمُ: The greeting or salutation (typically referring to the recitation of 'Assalamu alayna wa ala 'ibadillahis-salihin' or similar phrases) during prayer.
key_terms.الرَّاقِدَ: The sleeper or one who is dozing, referring to the state of the worshipper during prayer.
key_terms.بِالْحَاجَةِ: With the need, referring to the supplication or specific intentions of the prayer.
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْوَتْرِ: The two rak'ahs of the Witr prayer, a recommended night prayer.

ai.seo_question: What is the purpose of the greeting in the two rak'ahs of Witr prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar inquires of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the etiquette of the salutation in the two rak'ahs of Witr, to which the Imam responds that its primary function is to 'awaken the sleeper' and 'address the need.' This highlights the practical spiritual dimension of Witr, emphasizing mindfulness and the transition from the day's activities to a focused state of supplication before sleep or night prayer.
